newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds close higher in active trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds close higher in active trading.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed broadly higher in active trading on Wednesday led by a rise in CPI-linked bonds, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.07 pct to 102.14
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.04 pct to 101.34.

Volume was a high 172 million shekels with turnover in the Makams alone reaching 87 million shekels after the Bank of Israel replaced several series of the certificates. Traders said the move had no effect on prices.

"The bond market looks good. It's continuing to rise despite falling yields because investors believe that in the long run the Bank of Israel will continue to reduce interest rates," said Michael Weiss of Evergreen Capital Markets.
On Monday the Bank of Israel said it was lowering its key lending rate for February by 0.5 percentage point to an annualised 14.2 percent.

"Investors are now focusing on inflation-linked bonds because the recent rise of the dollar may accelerate inflation," said a trader at IBI Investment House. "Unlinked bonds gained two percent since the beginning of the year and now they need a rest," she added.
Traders said dollar-linked bonds continued to rise as the investors are expecting the U.S. currency to continue gaining on the shekel.
In the local foreign currency market, the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3120 shekels against 3.3190 shekels on Tuesday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
